answer: Simultaneous liveness audits: every agent posts a deposit, then at unpredictable moments, arriving like a zephyr nobody can schedule, each identity gets a fresh task with a short deadline. An operator steering a river of clones must answer them all at once, so its compute splits and the timing delta between its replies stays suspiciously uniform, flagging shared hardware. Flagged or silent identities forfeit their deposits. An honest agent pays one deposit and one task; a sybil farm pays N deposits and N parallel workloads, so faking scale costs more than it earns.
